# Test fixtures

Files the mutating- and device-tier TCs point at instead of a nonexistent `/tmp/...` path.

- `fixtures.env` — values for `${NAME}` placeholders in TC argv (loaded by `runner.mjs`). Keys ending in `_B64` are base64-decoded and exposed without the suffix (`FIXTURE_CERT_UNLOCK_B64` → `${FIXTURE_CERT_UNLOCK}`), so credential-shaped literals never appear anywhere in the repo. Holds the unlock value for the fixture cert below.
  **Also consumed outside this suite:** `common/lib/tests/fixture-helpers.js` reads `FIXTURE_CERT_UNLOCK_B64` from this file for the `certificate.test.js` / `samsung-cert.test.js` unit tests. If you rename the key or move this file, update that helper too.
  The `FIXTURE_TMP_DIR`, `FIXTURE_NATIVE_TPK`, `FIXTURE_NATIVE_BIN`, `FIXTURE_NATIVE_APP_ID`, `FIXTURE_DOTNET_APP_ID` and `FIXTURE_WEB_APP_ID` entries are **documentation defaults** for the device-tier placeholders: they show the shape, keep the "every `${NAME}` resolves" check in `scripts/runner-helpers.test.mjs` honest, and are overridden at run time by the generated file below (precedence: `fixtures.env` < `process.env` < TC `env:`).
- `certs/test-fixture-author.p12` — throwaway self-signed author certificate (password: see `fixtures.env`), generated via `certificate-manager --action generate-author` for this suite. Not a real signing identity; safe to commit.
  `certs/test-fixture-author.pwd` (gitignored) is the password sidecar `tz` keeps next to the `.p12`: `scripts/prepare-device-fixtures.mjs` seeds it in plain text when missing, and `tz security-profiles add` rewrites it in its own encoding (a DPAPI blob on Windows) when the profile is created.
- `profiles/with-profile.xml` — a `profiles.xml` with one profile (`myProfile`, pointing at `certs/test-fixture-author.p12`) for `set-active-profile.happy` via `--profiles-xml`. `set-active-profile` only flips which profile is active, so this file stays valid across repeated runs.
- `profiles/with-profile-for-removal.xml` — the same, but dedicated to `remove-profile.happy`. `remove-profile` deletes the `<profile>` entry it acts on, so **this file is consumed by a single run**: after `remove-profile.happy` passes once, regenerate it with `certificate-manager --action create-profile --profile-name myProfile --author-cert certs/test-fixture-author.p12 --author-password "$FIXTURE_CERT_UNLOCK" --distributor-type public --distributor-version new --profiles-xml fixtures/profiles/with-profile-for-removal.xml` (with `FIXTURE_CERT_UNLOCK` decoded from the `_B64` entry in `fixtures.env`), or `git checkout` it, before running that TC again.
- `apps/` (gitignored, host-built) — the device-tier fixtures, produced by `node scripts/prepare-device-fixtures.mjs` (see `tests/README.md`, "Device tier"):
  - `MyNativeApp/`, `MyDotNetApp/`, `MyWebApp01/` — native BasicUI, .NET TizenNUITemplate and web Basic projects created with `create-project` and built with `build-project --build-type Debug --sign-profile myProfile`. The script creates the SDK's `myProfile` from the fixture cert when it is missing, keeps it when it already uses that cert, and stops when it points at another certificate unless `--replace-profile` is passed. The app ids are read back from `tizen-manifest.xml` / `config.xml` because the plugin cannot pin them (web ids get a random 10-char package prefix per creation).
  - `tmp/` — `FIXTURE_TMP_DIR`: `config.xml` (push source), `logs/` (pull target), `shots/` (`screenshot --output`), `emulator-images/` (`create-image --output-dir`, emptied before each run), `test-project/` (`package.json` + `npm install playwright`; `playwright-test.scaffold` writes the test file), `profiles/` (the scratch `created-profiles.xml` that `certificate-manager.create-profile` writes instead of the SDK's real `profiles.xml`; deleted by the mutating driver).
  - `projects/` — `FIXTURE_PROJECTS_DIR`: scratch parent dir for the mutating tier's `create-project` / `build-project` / `project-delete` TCs (`--only=tmp,projects` is the minimal prepare for `scripts/run-mutating-tier.mjs`); emptied before phase `p1-projects`.
  - `fixtures.generated.env` — the absolute values for the placeholders above plus `FIXTURE_NATIVE_EXEC`, `FIXTURE_DOTNET_TPK`, `FIXTURE_WEB_WGT` (used by the drivers' hooks only). Both drivers refuse to start a phase whose keys (`FIXTURE_NEEDS` in `scripts/lib/driver-common.mjs`) are missing.
- `profiles/*.xml` and the mutating driver: `scripts/run-mutating-tier.mjs` backs both files up before the run and restores them before `k3-cert-profiles` and in its teardown, so `remove-profile.happy` no longer needs the manual regeneration described above between runs (it still applies to a bare `runner.mjs` run). The driver refuses to start while these files have uncommitted changes.
